headline: The transcription work in programs.md holds up under re-reading; three independent image reads this pass produced zero disagreements with its wire lists. What does not hold up is (a) a contact-polarity cell and an open question that the Maintenance Manual settled and nobody carried back into this file, (b) an errata note assigned to three flip-flops when it belongs to exactly one, (c) two Tic-Tac-Toe items left open that the panel photograph closed, and (d) the absence of the three Maintenance Manual check circuits, which are the best combinational fixtures in the whole package and are not in the corpus at all.

Replace with: | Relay `n`, second contact set | `nL` | `nK` (closes when relay is ON) | `nN` (opens when relay is ON) | not settled |, and tag the three terminal roles [verified] with the source below. rulings.evidence: maintenance-manual.pdf printed p.7 = PDF p.9, 'Circuit Diagram — Relay Check', rendered by me at 400 dpi. The figure wires + to H, + to L and + to Y; J to 1A, G to 2A, N to 3A, K to 4A; 1B/2B/3B/4B to the minus terminals; the coil is driven from the pushbutton's X terminal, and the arms are drawn at rest touching J, N and Z. Relay de-energised therefore conducts through J and N; relay energised conducts through G and K. rulings.section: §2.2 Conformance seed set — tier A, and a new subsection under §4

rulings.ruling: ADD the three Maintenance Manual check circuits as corpus records and put them at the head of the tier-A seed set. Each is a complete printed netlist with SDC's own printed expected lamp states, no relay chain, no motor, no rotary — a better conformance floor than anything currently in tier A. (1) `MM-PB-CHECK`, MAINT printed p.6-7 = PDF p.8-9, 5 wires: `+/Y`, `Z/1A`, `1B/1-`, `X/2A`, `2B/2-`; printed expected 'Turn power on. Light 1 should come on. Push the pushbutton. (2) `MM-RLY-CHECK`, MAINT printed p.7 = PDF p.9, 13 wires: `+/H`, `+/L`, `+/Y`, `X/E`, `F/-`, `J/1A`, `1B/1-`, `G/2A`, `2B/2-`, `N/3A`, `3B/3-`, `K/4A`, `4B/4-`, with `C` and `Z` deliberately unconnected; printed expected 'Turn power on. Lights 1 and 3 should come on. Push the pushbutton. Lights 1 and 3 should go off and lights 2 and 4 should come on.' Record the coil-driven-at-E consequence: the relay's own indicator lamp is out of circuit and stays DARK in this fixture. (3) `MM-SW-CHECK`, MAINT printed p.8 = PDF p.10, 10 wires: `+/S`, `+/V`, `T/1A`, `1B/1-`, `R/2A`, `2B/2-`, `W/3A`, `3B/3-`, `U/4A`, `4B/4-`; printed expected 'Set the slide switch RIGHT. Also record the FIG-PB printing error as printed, not fixed: the page prints '2B' on BOTH terminals of light 2; the intended left-hand label is `2A` (printed-[verified]; correction [likely], from the correctly-labelled `1A (lamp) 1B` on the same figure and all four lamps on the Relay Check figure). rulings.currentText: **Best-specified combinational fixture in the corpus** — five printed numbered steps, each with a stated relay-3 outcome. The numbered steps are on printed p.14 (PDF p.20), not p.13 where the heading sits.
rulings.ruling: ADD the structural fact this record is silent about. Its first three wires `1+/1H`, `1H/1L`, `1L/1X` contain an explicit `1H`-to-`1L` PROGRAMMING WIRE: SDC has to bridge the relay's two contact sets with a patch cord, which is direct printed evidence that the G/H/J set and the K/L/N set are electrically ISOLATED inside the relay. Name `II-EXP5` the isolation regression test in this record and in §2.2: a simulator that internally ties H to L passes all three Maintenance Manual check circuits (PR-03) and fails this one. The same bridge appears in `II-EXP6` (`1H/1L`), which is a second instance and should be cross-referenced.

rulings.section: §1 Tic-Tac-Toe — closing paragraph, and §5 row N-1
rulings.currentText: §1: 'The ring geometry is not settled by the sources. … Not settled by Book I, Book VI or the errata sheet — it has to come from the panel photograph. Fallback: none named here; do not ship a tic-tac-toe fixture that asserts a specific machine move until the panel file settles it.' §5 N-1: '**The ring order of the nine matrix squares** … | None. It must come from the panel photograph. Do not ship a Tic-Tac-Toe fixture that asserts a specific machine move until the panel file settles it. |'
rulings.ruling: SPLIT the question — half of it is settled, half of it needs a named default, and the file currently has no default at all, which breaches its own rule that every unsettled item names one. (a) The RING ORDER is settled [verified]: the eight outer squares run 1-2-3-4-5-6-7-8 clockwise from top-left around centre 9, read off the panel photograph; the panel file has done what N-1 said someone had to do. (b) What remains unsettled is the SEMANTICS of 'squares to the right' on that ring — the sign, and how the rule applies from the centre square, which is not on the ring at all. Rewrite N-1 as: 'Not settled: what "move 5 squares to the right" / "move 4 squares to the right" means as an operation on the ring, and how the rule is anchored when the machine's last move was the centre. Book VI states the rule and never defines "right"; the errata sheet adds only ER-44. **Named default `FALLBACK-TTT-RING-CW`:** "N squares to the right" = advance N positions in the printed numbering modulo 8 around the outer ring (1→2→…→8→1), because the panel's own numbering runs clockwise from top-left and is the only cyclic order the machine physically expresses. Every step generated under it carries tag [unverified] and source `FALLBACK-TTT-RING-CW`. Keep the standing caution: do not ship a Tic-Tac-Toe fixture that asserts a specific machine move on the strength of the default alone.' Make the §1 paragraph agree with the rewritten N-1.
rulings.evidence: Ring order: as PR-10 (my own read of raw/photos/commons-minivac601-main.jpg; panel.md line 348; find-panel claims[33]; critic C8). rulings.section: §0 How to read this file (or a new §6 item) — no consolidated entry exists
rulings.currentText: The free-ended wire is flagged four separate times and never in one place: §1's per-line table ('The simulator needs a first-class "touch a terminal with a loose wire end" input'), §2.4's `VI-MAZE` row ('needs the loose-wire-touch input'), `V-EXP12`'s closing line ('eight loose-ended wires'), and `V-MAZESOLVER`'s closing line ('Uses a **loose-ended wire** at `6E`').
rulings.ruling: ADD one consolidated entry naming all four programs, so the simulator requirement is stated once as a requirement rather than four times as an aside. 'FREE-ENDED WIRES — a first-class input, not a patch cord. Four programs wire one end of a programming wire to a terminal and leave the other end loose for the operator to relocate at run time: `VI-TICTACTOE` (`M10/free`, the machine's play wire; `M11/free`, the player's), `V-EXP12` Arabic Numeral Recognition (four free wires on `M10` and four on `M11`), `V-MAZESOLVER` (`6E`, moved between `D3`, `D5` and `D7` to nominate the goal), `VI-MAZE` (a wire at `M+`, the play wire). None of these is a jack-to-jack connection and none can be represented as one. Book VI prints the proof for the maze, verbatim: "(The wire need not be plugged into the terminal; touching the terminal will make the contact.)" That sentence is printed only for `VI-MAZE`; Tic-Tac-Toe's own procedure says "place the free end … in 6 com", i.e. insertion. So the general requirement is a wire with one free end the operator moves at run time; momentary touch without insertion is the `VI-MAZE` special case, and whether it is also how the other three are meant to be operated is [unverified].' Keep the four per-program flags where they are.

Also, connect four short programming wires to M11, leaving one end of each free.' `V-MAZESOLVER` footnote, verbatim in the file: 'This programming wire may be connected to D3, D5 or D7 to indicate the goal.' The four-program tally is also stated once in raw/find-programs.json (the 'Four Book V/VI programs use a free-ended play wire' note) and nowhere in programs.md.
